idea: A dog-walking app for busy Madrid professionals, €12 a walk

mia.title: Dog-walking service in Madrid
mia.one_liner: The same trusted walker every weekday at midday, booked in two taps.

brief.concept: Vetted walkers doing 45-minute midday walks in Chamberí, booked through a simple page, €12 a group walk.
brief.for: Office workers aged 28 to 45 in Chamberí who leave a dog home alone from 9:00 to 18:00.
brief.goal: Get 25 owners to pay for a first walk and keep 10 on weekly plans after four weeks.

checklist.task: Interview 15 owners in two Chamberí parks
checklist.how: Talk to owners at 8:00 and 20:00 about who walked their dog last week and what it cost.

checklist.task: Map the walkers owners already use
checklist.how: Ask every owner for their walker's price, frequency and last no-show.

checklist.task: Recruit three walkers for a paid trial
checklist.how: Post in two local groups and meet each candidate in a park with their own dog.
checklist.done_when: Three walkers signed for a trial week

checklist.task: Get two walker liability insurance quotes
checklist.how: Ask two brokers for cover per walker and per dog, group walks included.
First walk free for interviewed owners, €12 from the second; one walker, three dogs max.

checklist.task: Pick the name and print 100 collar tags
checklist.how: Choose one of Nova's names and hand tags to every trial owner.

checklist.task: Send the booking page to 60 owners
checklist.how: Message every owner met so far and two neighbourhood groups.

checklist.task: Post the first three launch posts
checklist.how: Share walk photos with owner permission on the planned days.
checklist.done_when: Three posts live; every message answered

checklist.how: Follow up personally with every owner who opened the page.
Compare repeat bookings and walker hours with break-even and the kill criteria.
checklist.done_when: Decision written down with the numbers

leo.headline: Win one neighbourhood, not the whole city.
leo.summary: Owners already pay for walks, but large pet-sitting platforms cover all of Madrid. A dense, trusted service in one neighbourhood is winnable; a city-wide app is not.

signals.name: Demand
signals.why: Many owners leave dogs alone through office hours

signals.name: Competition gap
signals.why: Big platforms and independents already cover the city

signals.name: Channel
signals.why: Parks, vets and pet shops reach owners cheaply

signals.name: Timing
signals.why: Hybrid work thins Monday and Friday demand

leo.why_go: Trust is local: the same walker in one neighbourhood every weekday beats a marketplace that sends a stranger.

risks.risk: Platforms already list hundreds of walkers here.
risks.mitigation: Stay in Chamberí; same walker, same time, every day.

risks.risk: One walker no-show breaks trust fast.
risks.mitigation: Keep a back-up walker on call during the trial.

risks.risk: Hybrid work halves Monday and Friday bookings.

pivot.idea: Group midday walks in Chamberí, sold as a weekly plan, no app.
pivot.why: Fixes the competition gap: platforms sell single walks with strangers; a fixed weekly group with the same walker is different and cheaper per dog.

leo.next_step: Interview 15 owners in two Chamberí parks this week: 6 who pay today is the bar.

market_facts.fact: Central Madrid dog walks commonly cost €10 to €15 for 30 to 60 minutes.
Owners in office jobs typically leave a dog alone for 7 to 9 hours.
A walker can usually handle 3 to 4 compatible dogs on a group walk.
Walker liability insurance is usually priced per walker and per dog.

competitors.name: Pet-sitting marketplaces
competitors.note: Huge choice, a new face each time

competitors.name: Independent local walkers
competitors.note: Trusted, but full and hard to book

competitors.name: Dog daycare centres
competitors.note: Full day, pricey, far from home

interviews.who: Dog owners in Chamberí who work office hours
interviews.where: Two parks at 8:00 and 20:00, and outside two vets
questions: Who walked your dog last Tuesday at midday?
What did you pay for the last walk?
Tell me about the last time a walk didn't happen.
How do you book a walk today?
interviews.good_sign: They pay someone already and can name a missed walk this month.

kill_criteria: Stop if fewer than 6 of 15 owners pay for walks today.
Stop if under 8 of 20 trial walks convert to paid.
leo.verdict_rule: Go from 7.0 with no signal at 3 or below · Pivot 5.0–6.9 · No-go under 5.0

confidence.note: Desk estimates only, no web sources: signals capped at 7.5. Interviews decide.

memo.purpose: Midday group walks with the same trusted walker, for office workers in one Madrid neighbourhood.
memo.problem: Owners who work office hours leave dogs alone for up to nine hours. Marketplaces send a different stranger each time, and good independent walkers are full.
memo.insight: A city-wide app loses to platforms that already exist. A weekly group in one neighbourhood, with the same face every day, is something they don't offer.
memo.verdict_line: Pivot to one neighbourhood: break-even is about 24 walks a day, which needs four steady walkers.
